title: Demurrage and Detention Free Time: Detention Days Billed Beyond Free Time
content:
This page defines which days a Demurrage and Detention Free Time record bills as detention on its final detention line, and which dates that line opens and closes on.

## Products on separate clocks

| Direction | Detention clock starts | Detention clock stops | Free days compared |
|---|---|---|---|
| import | full gate-out date | empty return date | the product's import detention free days |
| export | empty pickup date | full gate-in date | the product's export detention free days |

A clock's used days number the calendar days between its start date and its stop date. The detention days billed are those days used that lie beyond the free days, and there are none when the days used do not exceed the free days.

## Products on a combined clock

On import, the single merged clock covers the span from the discharge date to the day the empty comes back; on export, from the day the empty is picked up to the loading date. It is measured against the merged free days for the record's direction. Its n-th day is the date reached by adding n calendar days to the start date.

- On an **import** record, every day later than the full gate-out date counts as detention.
- On an **export** record, each day no later than the full gate-in date counts as detention.

Under a merged clock the line bills every day that is both chargeable, lying past the merged free days, and a detention day. Put by position: on import they are the days whose position exceeds both the free days and the position of the full gate-out date; on export they are the days whose position exceeds the free days but does not exceed the position of the full gate-in date.

## Dates on the line

The line's opening and closing dates are simply the earliest and the latest chargeable detention day. So where the last billed detention day coincides with a terminal movement — the full gate-in of an export container on a merged clock, for instance — the line closes on the date of that movement and not on the date on which the record's charges stopped accruing.

## Worked cases (hypothetical dates and free days)

| Case | Clock | Days used | Free days | Detention days billed | Line runs |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| separate, import: gate-out 9 May, empty back 20 May | 9 May to 20 May | 11 | 3 | 8 | 13 May to 20 May |
| merged, export: pickup 1 June, gate-in 20 June, loaded 28 June | 1 June to 28 June | 27 | 10 | 9, positions 11 to 19 | 12 June to 20 June |
| merged, import: discharge 1 June, gate-out 8 June, empty back 25 June | 1 June to 25 June | 24 | 10 | 14, positions 11 to 24 | 12 June to 25 June |

In the export case the full gate-in date is position 19, so positions 20 to 27 are not detention days. In the merged import case the full gate-out date is position 7, below the free days, so detention begins at position 11.
